title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level network configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents; model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate; repair budget ≤1 per intent. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Execution accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize the methodological lesson that baseline calibration is necessary to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution artifacts, model-configuration metadata, and analysis code are archived in the execution bundle; preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce operator burden by expressing desired network changes in free text and automatically translating those intents into executable low-level device configurations. Prior work shows single-pass LLM outputs frequently contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states when applied without verification [1],[2],[3]. A standard defensive pattern is a generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline: an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and an automated repair or manual gate corrects violations before execution [4],[5]. Security analyses of tool-augmented LLM agents further motivate deterministic gating since unchecked textual claims can be converted into harmful actions in multi-tool workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review we preregistered the confirmatory question tested here: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The preregistered trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) froze tasks, inclusion/exclusion rules, analysis plan, and execution semantics before any model calls.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial on a deterministically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents) comparing baseline free-text prompting to constrained prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete, artifact-backed numerical results showing a near-ceiling baseline (149/150) and a guarded marginal increase to 150/150 (absolute +0.67 pp), with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02]. (3) A concrete methodological recommendation: short baseline-calibration pilots are essential for preregistered NetOps trials to avoid ceiling effects and to choose N and task difficulty consistent with targeted detectable effects. We also report full execution accounting (model_calls_used = 151, repair invocations = 1) and precise runtime sampling metadata recorded in the archived model_configuration.json.
sections.related_work:
Three strands frame our study. First, intent-to-configuration research documents the difficulty of producing verifier-sound formal artifacts from free text and reports modest semantic-correctness on public and synthetic benchmarks, motivating post-generation checks and verifier-aware pipelines [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures and verifier-guided training (for IaC and configuration repair) have shown correctness improvements, but gains vary with baseline model competence, repair budget, and sampling semantics [4],[7]. Third, security and systems analyses demonstrate claim-to-action risks for tool-augmented LLM agents and argue for auditable gating and verifier-aware planning to limit exploitation [6],[8].

How this work differs. Prior studies that report larger guarded-vs-baseline gains often operate under different execution semantics (independent per-condition sampling), allow larger repair budgets, or compare models with lower baseline competence. Our experiment isolates the marginal value of a single repair applied to an identical initial sampled candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) using a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). This narrower operational estimand bounds the marginal runtime benefit of lightweight guarded pipelines in a low-variance sampling regime and demonstrates how differing semantics change inferential meaning.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and the analysis plan frozen prior to any model interaction (preregistration SHA-256 archived in the execution manifest). Design: paired_binary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) with an exact two-sided McNemar test as primary confirmatory inference and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Planned confirmatory sample: N=150 paired intents (planned episodes = 300). The preregistration specified inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector and verifier-coverage checks), retry policy (one deterministic retry on API timeout), and a power plan targeting an absolute +15 pp improvement with ≈80% power under conservative discordant assumptions. The preregistration, analysis code, and execution contract are archived; preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by the preregistered generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with recorded generation seeds. The task bank spans four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests were run; no confirmatory exclusions occurred (exclusions = 0). Representative task manifests archived in the bundle include difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard) and explicit required_sequence constraints to ensure nontrivial workflows.

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair call budget per intent. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied full_intent_constraint_validation and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration text and diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). Important runtime-parameter clarification required by review and incorporated here: the archived execution model_configuration.json explicitly records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). No numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced; thus model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. The model_configuration.json and per-call runtime metadata are archived for inspection.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and estimand interpretation. The adapter used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, (a) the baseline success rate measures the validity of that single initial sampled candidate, and (b) the guarded vs baseline contrast isolates the marginal effect of at most one repair applied to the same candidate. This differs from independent-sampling designs where per-condition randomness yields different estimands (average over independent draws) and can allow larger observable differences.

Execution accounting, contamination controls, and scoring. Planned episodes = 300; completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. Provider audit recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call) and artifact_hash_count = 1058. The adapter enforced fresh API sessions per call to prevent session leakage; contamination_summary.csv shows no contamination flags. Primary outcome: deterministic verifier pass/fail (binary). Primary analysis: exact two-sided McNemar test on paired contingency counts with 95% bootstrap percentile CI computed using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness policy and sensitivity analyses were preregistered; no missingness occurred and sensitivity analyses were not needed.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. The deterministic reconciliation artifact reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and condition_counts: {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero contamination flags.

Primary numerical outcomes and paired contingency. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Observed paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These numerical facts are drawn directly from analysis/results.json and archived condition_summary and paired_contingency_table artifacts.

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), converting an initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for every episode provide validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flag; representative traces (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json) show nontrivial intent patterns and the validator's normalization behavior.

Representative examples and difficulty. Representative task manifests and shared-initial responses substantiate that the generator produced nontrivial workflows. Example (task-000001): intent — "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the four-command sequence expected by the reference answer; validator diagnostics recorded parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and valid = true. Other representative tasks (000002–000006) demonstrate medium-to-very_hard difficulty labels with required sequences ranging from 2 to 6 commands, yet the tested model achieved near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No parser mapping failures, verifier-unsupported cases, or pre-execution unit-test failures occurred; exclusions = 0. Contamination and mapping unit-tests passed before batch execution.
sections.discussion:
Numerical interpretation and ceiling effect. The guarded pipeline's observed marginal gain (~0.67 pp) is numerically tiny and statistically non-significant under the preregistered test. The primary experimental constraint was a near-ceiling baseline (baseline_success_rate = 0.9933), which eliminated most headroom for the guarded repair to demonstrate a large absolute improvement. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline (detectable +15 pp), so the realized baseline produced a classic ceiling-effect mismatch between assumptions and observed data. Practitioners should run baseline-calibration pilots to estimate model competence and set N and task difficulty consistent with targeted detectable effects.

Semantics, estimands, and experimental design implications. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline measures a single sampled candidate's validity and the guarded condition isolates the marginal value of at most one repair to that candidate. Independent-sampling semantics or larger repair budgets change the estimand to average performance over independent draws or cumulative repair-driven robustness gains; such designs typically permit larger observable differences. Our result therefore bounds the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded workflow in a low-variance sampling regime for gpt-5-mini on this frozen synthetic corpus.

Operational implications beyond binary pass/fail. Deterministic guarded workflows produce operational artifacts not captured by a binary metric: (1) normalized, auditable configuration text suitable for human review; (2) standardized repair prompts and repair traces that support triage; and (3) deterministic verifier diagnostics (violation codes, parsed_command_count) that can feed gating and rollback policies. These operational affordances can justify guarded architectures even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small on constrained corpora.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics reduce sampling variance but do not capture condition-level randomness; adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audit mitigate cross-condition leakage (cross_condition_cache_reuse_observed = false). Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; mapping unit-tests were applied pre-execution and mapping artifacts archived, but residual risk remains. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic small-topology tasks limit production generality. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions were invalid due to higher-than-expected baseline performance; reported p-values and CIs reflect the observed data without overclaiming.

Recommendations for future preregistered NetOps trials. Based on the archived artifacts we recommend: (1) perform a brief baseline-calibration pilot prior to fixing N to estimate baseline competence for the chosen model and prompt style; (2) state generation semantics explicitly (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) in preregistration because semantics change the estimand; (3) preregister repair-budget sensitivity analyses; (4) archive and run mapping/verifier unit-tests prior to batch runs to avoid post-hoc exclusions; and (5) report provider-call audits (model_calls_used, stage_counts, cache_miss/hit) to document execution budgets and stage-level behavior.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting to constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministically generated synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials require baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
